opportunities.title: User creation endpoint has no input validation
opportunities.summary: ## Bug: Missing Input Validation on User Creation **Description:** The `POST /api/users` endpoint does not validate input with Zod schema, unlike auth and job routes which use proper validation. This allows arbitrary data to be stored as user records. **File:** `apps/api/src/controllers/userController.js` **Current code:** ```js export async function postUser(req, res) { return ok(res, await createUser(req.body), 201); } ``` **Expected behavior:** A Zod validation schema should be created for user creation (similar to `registerSchema` and `createJobSchema`) and applied before passing data to the service layer. **Impact:** Medium — allows malformed or malicious data to be persisted as user records. This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. opportunities.title: auth refresh endpoint issues tokens without verifying the requester
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `POST /api/auth/refresh` currently issues a fresh access token without checking the requester at all. The service also signs that token for the hard-coded subject `usr_existing` with role `client`, so even an authenticated caller does not get a token for their own subject and role. ## Expected fix Protect the refresh route with the existing bearer-token auth middleware, pass the verified user payload into the refresh service, and sign the refreshed token for that authenticated subject and role. Add route-level tests for unauthenticated rejection and authenticated subject preservation. ## Scope This issue is limited to the auth refresh route/service behavior for `/api/auth/refresh` and focused API tests. This issue is limited only to the creator of this issue. This means that only the issue author can attempt to solve this issue. If you would like to work on it, please create another issue with the same contents and refer to issue #743 for more information. References #743.

opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
